METHOD AND DEVICE FOR THE APPLICATION OF REFLECTING MATERIAL ON A SUBSTRATE

abstract.p: Method for the application of reflecting material on a substrate, in particular of a reflecting strip on a band (3), characterised in that on the place where the reflecting material is to be provided, a layer (23) of a polymer solution with at least one pigment and a second layer (24) with light-reflecting particles are applied on the substrate. The device contains two nozzles (4 and 5), means for successively moving a band (3) in relation to said two nozzles (4 and 5) and heating means for heating the band (3) beyond each nozzle (4-5).

L'invention concerne un procédé permettant d'appliquer une matière réfléchissante sur un substrat, plus particulièrement un film réfléchissant sur une bande (3). A cet effet, on enduite le substrat à l'endroit où la matière réfléchissante doit être déposée, une couche (23) d'une solution polymère comprenant au moins un pigment et une seconde couche (24) renfermant des particules réfléchissantes à la lumière. Ce dispositif comprend deux ajutages (4, 5), des moyens de déplacement d'une bande (3) par rapport à ces deux ajutages (4, 5) et des moyens chauffants permettant de chauffer la bande (3) au-delà de chaque ajutage (4-5).

description.p: Method and device for the application of reflecting material on a substrate.
The present invention concerns a method for the application of reflecting material on a substrate, preferably a flexible substrate, m particular of a reflecting strip on a band .
The material can have purely reflecting qualities or reflecting qualities m combination with phosphorescent or fluorescent qualities.
According to known methods, a prefabricated reflecting ribbon is attached on clothes or such by means of stitching, gluing or welding.
This method is relatively time-consuming, since a reflecting ribbon has to be fabricated first, after which this ribbon is to be provided on a substrate such as a garment or band.
Other known methods consist in providing reflecting material on a substrate by means of transfer, for example under the influence of heat.

These methods are complicated and time-consuming as well, since the material to be transferred has to be provided on a substrate first, after which this material has to be provided on the eventual substrate by means of transfer. This usually requires a relatively expensive machine and a special composition of the material to be transferred. Moreover, the first substrate upon which the material to be
transferred has been provided constitutes a relatively large amount of waste .
The invention aims to avoid these disadvantages and to provide a method for applying reflecting material on a band which is relatively simple, fast and flexible.

This aim is reached according to the invention m that on the place where the reflecting material is to be provided, a layer of a polymer solution with at least one pigment and a second layer with light-reflecting particles are applied on the substrate.
Preferably, the second layer is provided m a liquid form after the first layer has dried.
According to a special embodiment, after this second layer has dried, the two layers are levelled under pressure as a whole .
The substrate is preferably a band, m particular a fabric, and the reflecting material is provided on it as a strip.
The two layers can be levelled by calendering the substrate and the layers as a whole .
This calendering preferably takes place between two rollers, whereby the roller situated on the side of the layers is driven at a higher peripheral velocity than the other one .

In order to accelerate the drying of an applied layer, this layer can be heated. If the first layer is heated, this layer is preferably cooled before the second one is
provided. When the second layer is heated before it is dried, it is preferably cooled before it is levelled.

The first layer may be an acrylic polyurethane or an acrylic vinyl acetate on an aqueous base onto which pigment has been added, and the second layer may be a transparent layer consisting of a resin with reflecting particles added to it, m particular glass beads.
The invention also concerns a device which is suitable for applying the method according to any of the preceding embodiments on band-shaped substrates.

The invention thus concerns a device for applying a strip of reflecting material on a band, which device contains two liquid supply systems, means for successively moving a band m relation to said two liquid supply systems and heating means for heating the band beyond each liquid supply system.
Practically, the device contains at least one calender through which the band can be guided for levelling and smoothing the layers provided by the liquid supply systems.
The calender contains two rollers and means for driving at least one of these rollers, such that the one roller turns at a higher peripheral velocity than the other one.
Preferably, the heating means contain two rotating, heated drums over which the band is guided, whereby at least the second liquid supply system is erected opposite to this pair of drums .

The two drums may have converging axes, such that the band automatically advances towards the end where the axes are
situated closest to one another when the band is guided over these drums .

In order to better explain the characteristics of the invention, the following preferred embodiments of a method and a device for applying a reflecting material on a substrate according to the invention are described as an example only without being limitative in any way, with reference to the accompanying drawings, in which:

figure 1 schematically represents a side view of a device for applying a strip of reflecting material on a band according to the invention; figure 2 schematically represents a top view of the device of figure 1; figures 3 and 4 represent the parts indicated by F3 and F4 in figure 1 to a larger scale; figures 5 to 7 also represent the parts indicated by
F5 , F6 and F7 respectively in figure 2 to a larger scale; figure 8 represents a part analogous to that in figure
3 , but with reference to another embodiment of the invention; figure 9 represents the part analogous to that in figure 8, but with reference to yet another embodiment .

In order to apply a reflecting material according to the invention, two layers are successively provided on a substrate, formed of a basic fabric in the given example, woven with a fine structure and made of UV-resistant synthetic material, in particular polyester.

The first layer is made of a polymer solution, consisting of acrylic polyurethane or acrylic vinyl acetate on an
aqueous base onto which have been added one or several pigments, in particular colour pigments and/or metal pigments
According to a variant, the pigments may entirely or partly consist of a phosphor or fluorescent material in case the reflecting strip also has to be phosphorescent or fluorescent .
This polymer solution is spread over the fabric m the required proportions, for example by immersion, by means of a nozzle, by means of a vibrating roller or by means of a spreader
This basic layer is subsequently dried, which can be accelerated by heating it

The second layer, which is preferably only provided after the first one has dried, is transparent and consists of light-reflecting particles, in particular glass beads, m a transparent base consisting of resin, polyurethane, polyvinyl chloride, acrylic or such on an aqueous base

This layer is dried and chemically stabilised, after which the entire coating provided on the fabric is levelled and smoothed by rolling said fabric with the two layers between two rollers, whereby the roller which makes contact with the coating is preferably driven at a higher peripheral velocity than the other one.

Immediately after the second layer has been applied, before it is dried, the substrate with the two layers may be exposed to ultrasonic vibrations, as a result of which the light-reflecting particles will emerge on the surface of
the second layer, which results m a larger reflection of reflecting material.

The above-described method is particularly suitable for applying a strip of reflecting material on a woven band, whereoy the layers can be applied, dried and levelled while the band is unrolled from one roller and rolled up on another one .
Figures 1 to 7 represent a device which is designed for applying a strip on a band m such a way.

This device mainly consists of a frame 1, a feed mechanism 2 for a woven band 3, two liquid supply systems formed of nozzles 4 and 5 for applying the two above-mentioned layers, means consisting of two internally heated drums 6 and 7 for heating the band 3 beyond each nozzle 4 and 5, a cooling part 8, a calender 9 and a roll-up mechanism 10.

The feed mechanism 2 consists of a roller holder 11 for a spool 12 upon which the band 3 is wound, and two guide rollers 13 and 14 which are pressed against one another and which are mounted such on the frame 1 that they turn loosely.

The two drums 6 and 7, which are significantly longer than the width of the band 3 , are bearing-mounted m the frame 1, such that they extend m the cross direction of the device and are situated opposite to the feed mechanism 2

As is represented m figure 2, the axes of the two drums 6 and 7 are not parallel to one another, by they converge towards their other end.
These drums 6 and 7 are hollow and can be heated by means of for example hot air or steam which is led through it.

The nozzle 4 is fixed on the frame 1 above the path of the band 3 between said feed mechanism 2 and the first drum 6, opposite one end of this drum 6, and in the given example it has a nozzle opening which is narrower than the band 3.
The nozzle 5 is identical, but it is attached to the frame 1 practically halfway down the length of this drum 6 above the path of the band 3.

The cooling part 8 consists of a number of conductors, for example capstans 15, for the band 3 which are fixed to the frame 1 alternately above and beneath it and shifted m the cross direction of the device.

The calender 9 consists of two rollers 16 and 17 provided on top of one another on the frame 1. One of the rollers, i.e. the top roller 16 m the given example, is driven by an electric motor 18 as represented m figures 1 and 7.
The other roller 17 is driven via a transmission 19, as represented m figure 4, such that its peripheral velocity is lower.
The calender 9 also forms the transport device of the band

The roll-up mechanism 10 consists of a roller holder 20 for a spool 12 upon which the band 3 can be wound. This spool 12 can be locked on the shaft 21 of the roller holder 20, which is then driven by the above-mentioned motor 18, for example via a transmission 22.
A roller with band 3 is placed on the roller holder 11, and the band 3 is provided between the guide rollers 13 and 14, guided several times around the two drums 6 and 7 as a whole, up and down over the capstans 15 of the cooling parr 8 and finally through the calender 9 up to the spool 12 of the roll-up mechanism.
The heating of the drums 6 and 7 is turned on, the motor 18 is activated and the nozzles 4 and 5 are fed with the material for forming the two layers .
The band 3 is transported through the calender 9 and wound on the spool 12 of the roll-up mechanism.
The above-mentioned polymer solution is squirted as a first layer 23 in the shape of a continuous strip on the band 3 by the first nozzle 4, as is represented m detail m figure 5.
This paste is dried on the heated drums 6 and 7.

As the axes of these drums 6 and 7 converge, successive windings of the band 3 around these drums 6 and 7 will automatically advance towards the end where the axes are situated closest to one another.

By the time the material squirted on the band 3 reaches the nozzle 5, it is dry. A second layer 24 of the above- mentioned material with reflecting particles is then squirted on the first layer 23 by the nozzle 5 m the shape of a strip having for example the same width.

When this material reaches the end of the drums 6 and 7, it s dry.
The band 3 with the layers 23 and 24 on top of one another is still warm, but it is cooled by the air as it follows its path up and down in the cooling part 8.
The layers 23 and 24 are levelled and smoothened by the calender 9.
The above-described method is simple and versatile.
According to a variant, the band 3 with the two layers 23 and 24 is exposed to ultrasonic vibrations immediately beyond the nozzle 5, and thus while the layer 24 is still wet .
To this end, as is represented m figure 8, the device contains a plate 25 beyond the drum 6, on whose bottom is provided a generator of ultrasonic vibrations 26.

Thanks to the ultrasonic generator 26, the light-reflecting particles, for example the glass beads m the layer 24, will be carried to the surface, as a result of which a larger quantity of such particles will be situated on the surface, so that the reflecting qualities are improved.
The nozzle 5 for the squirting of the second layer 24 is fed with light-reflecting particles m a transparent base from a reservoir 27 via a pipe 28 in which is mounted a pump 29.
For clarity's sake, this reservoir 27 and this pipe 28 and pump 29 are not represented m figures 1 to 7.

On the side wall of the reservoir 27 may also be fixed, as represented m figure 8, a generator of ultrasonic vibrations 30.
Thanks to these ultrasonic vibrations, the reflecting particles will not deposit m the resin of the transparent base m the reservoir, but they will remain evenly distributed m this resin.

Also the nozzle 4 is connected to a reservoir 33 via a pipe 31 containing a pump 32. On this reservoir could be provided a generator of ultrasonic vibrations as well, for example m order to prevent the pigments from depositing m the polymer solution m this reservoir 33, but this is usually not necessary.
Said polymer solution and said resin with light-reflecting particles must not necessarily be provided by means of a nozzle 4 or 5. Other liquid supply systems, for example with rollers, are possible.
Figure 9 represents a vibrating roller system which is used as an alternative to the nozzle 5, but naturally such a system may also replace the nozzle 4.

The band 3 is guided over guide rollers 34 over a vibrating roller 35 which makes contact with a wetting roller 36 which is partially immersed in a reservoir 37 containing the polymer solution or the resin with light-reflecting particles. Also on this reservoir 37 can be provided a generator for ultrasonic vibrations 26 as represented m figure 9.

The width of the band 3 or of the layers 23 and 24 can be easily adjusted. Thus, the layers 23 and 24 may cover the entire width of the band 3.
The strip with the two layers 23-24 adheres very strongly to the band 3 and has excellent reflecting and possibly also phosphorescent qualities.
The band 3 can also be made of plastic foil instead of fabric .

The invention is by no means limited to the above-described embodiments represented in the accompanying drawings; on the contrary, such a method and device for the application of reflecting material on a substrate can be made in all sorts of variants while still remaining within the scope of the invention.

claim.claim-text: Claims .

1. Method for the application of reflecting material on a substrate, m particular of a reflecting strip on a band (3) , characterised m that on the place where the reflecting material is to be provided, a layer (23) of a polymer solution with at least one pigment and a second layer (24) with light-reflecting particles are applied on the substrate .
2. Method according to claim 1, characterised m that the second layer (24) is provided m a liquid form after the first layer (23) has dried.
3. Method according to claim 1 or 2 , characterised m that, after the second layer (24) has dried, the two layers (23 and 24) are levelled under pressure.
4. Method according to any of claims 1 to 3 , characterised m that the second layer (24) is exposed to ultrasonic vibrations while it is still wet.
5. Method according to any of claims 1 to 4 , characterised m that the substrate is a band (3) , m particular a fabric, and m that the reflecting material is provided on it as a strip.
6. Method according to claim 5, characterised m that the strip (23-24) is provided on a band (3) made of a polyester fabric .
7. Method according to claims 3 and 5, characterised m that the two layers (23 and 24) are levelled by calendering the whole of the substrate and the layers (23 and 24) .
8. Method according to claim 7, characterised m that the calendering takes place between two rollers (16 and 17), whereby the roller (16) situated on the side of the layers
(23 and 24) is driven at a higher peripheral velocity than the other one .
9. Method according to claim 2 or 3 , characterised m that n order to accelerate the drying of an applied layer (23 or 24) , this layer (23 or 24) is heated.
10. Method according to claims 2 and 9, characterised m that the first layer (23) is heated before it is dried, but is first cooled before the second layer (24) is provided.
11. Method according to claims 3 and 9, characterised m that the second layer (24) is heated before it is dried and is cooled before it is levelled.

12. Method according to any of the preceding claims, characterised m that the first layer (23) is an acrylic polyurethane or an acrylic vinyl acetate on an aqueous base onto which pigment has been added.

13. Method according to any of the preceding claims, characterised m that the second layer (24) is a transparent layer consisting of a resin with reflecting particles added to it, m particular glass beads.

14. Device for applying a strip (23-24) of reflecting material on a band (3), which device contains two liquid supply systems (4 and 5) , means for successively moving a
band (3) in relation to said two liquid supply systems (4 and 5) and heating means for heating the band (3) beyond each liquid supply system (4-5) .

15. Device according to claim 14, characterised in that it contains at least one calender (9) through which the band (3) can be guided for levelling and smoothing the layers (23-24) provided by the liquid supply systems (4-5) .

16. Device according to claim 15, characterised in that the calender (9) contains two rollers (16 and 17) and means for driving at least one of these rollers (16-17), such that one roller turns at a higher peripheral velocity than the other one .

17. Device according to any of claims 14 to 16, characterised in that the heating means contain two rotating, heated drums (6 and 7) over which the band (3) is guided, whereby at least the second liquid supply system (5) is erected opposite to this pair of drums (6 and 7) .

18. Device according to claim 17, characterised in that the two drums (6 and 7) have converging axes, such that the band (3) automatically advances towards the end where the axes are situated closest to one another when it is guided over these drums (6 and 7) .

19. Device according to claim 15, characterised in that it contains a cooling part (18) in between the heating means and the calender (9) which consists of conductors (15) for the band (3) which are situated alternately at the top and at the bottom.

20. Device according to any of claims 14 to 19, characterised in that it contains a plate (25) beyond the
second liquid supply system (5) upon which is provided a generator of ultrasonic vibrations (26) .

21. Device according to any of claims 14 to 20, characterised in that the second liquid supply system (5) contains a reservoir (27; 37) upon which is provided a generator of ultrasonic vibrations (26) .
